review_notes: Read the whole file and grepped the SeveralComplexVariables sources for the repeated continuity/rpow_const pattern. The repeated proof is three copies of one argument (circle integrability of ‖f z‖^p for analytic f on a closed ball). It is short, so the finding is borderline. The other candidates (the repeated abs_of_pos simpa and the nested CircleIntegrable const_smul and sub terms inside one proof) are within a single proof or are routine, so I did not report them. I did not compile any proposed replacement.

    exact (hf.continuousOn.mono sphere_subset_closedBall).norm.rpow_const

findings.problem: The same argument is written three times: analytic on the closed ball gives continuous on the sphere, then `.norm.rpow_const` with `Or.inr hp.le`, then `ContinuousOn.circleIntegrable`. It occurs once in the scalar theorem (lines 96-99) and twice in the bullets of the vector-valued theorem (lines 145-148), once for `hLf` and once for `hf`. The vector-valued version restates it in a slightly different `|>.circleIntegrable` form. The pattern appears again for other reasons in Subharmonic.lean:221 and :226, so it recurs across the development.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a private lemma before `norm_rpow_le_circleAverage_scalar`:

lemma circleIntegrable_norm_rpow {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℂ F] {f : ℂ → F} {c : ℂ} {R p : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) (hp : 0 < p) (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (closedBall c R)) : CircleIntegrable (fun z => ‖f z‖ ^ p) c R

Proof sketch: `((hf.continuousOn.mono sphere_subset_closedBall).norm.rpow_const (fun z _ => Or.inr hp.le)).circleIntegrable hR.le`. Then in the scalar theorem use `have hpow := circleIntegrable_norm_rpow hR hp hf`. In the vector theorem, replace the two bullets by `· exact circleIntegrable_norm_rpow hR hp hLf` and `· exact circleIntegrable_norm_rpow hR hp hf`. The hypotheses are the same as in the existing theorems: `hR`, `hp` and `hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (closedBall c R)`. The scalar case is the instance F = ℂ, and the imports are unchanged.
findings.benefit: The integrability argument is stated and maintained once. The main proofs then say only that the power is integrable, which makes the real work (Jensen, the tangent inequality, and the Hahn–Banach transfer) easier to follow. A later change to the continuity or integrability argument would touch one place, not three.
